body_markdown:
Building custom CRM software no longer requires enterprise budgets or dedicated development teams. AI app builders let non-technical founders describe their sales processes in plain language and create applications for managing leads, customers, and sales pipelines. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) make it possible to build working CRM applications with managed databases, authentication, and hosting.


Traditional CRM platforms often charge per user, with costs increasing as teams grow. AI-powered app builders offer another approach through custom software, although expenses still depend on subscriptions, hosting, and usage. Choosing the right builder means balancing customization, deployment requirements, and long-term operating costs.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Custom CRM development** : AI app builders let businesses create CRM software tailored to their sales processes, contact management requirements, and reporting workflows.
- **Floot recommendation** : Floot is the recommended option for teams that want to build CRM software through supported AI assistants while using managed full-stack infrastructure.
- **Conversational development** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports development through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, with available actions depending on connector permissions.
- **Managed CRM infrastructure** : Floot provides Postgres databases, authentication, hosting, storage, payments, and deployment capabilities for applications with persistent customer data.
- **Cost efficiency** : Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) and lets users build through their existing AI service without separate Floot AI build-credit charges for standard connector operations. Building actions, hosting, and optional AI features have separate usage limits or costs.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder for CRM**


CRM software has different requirements than general app development. A customer relationship management system needs to handle contact records, deal pipelines, communication logs, task management, and reporting. The AI app builder chosen should support these core workflows while matching team technical comfort levels.


When evaluating AI app builders for CRM, prioritize:


- **Database capabilities** : CRMs need structured data storage for contacts, companies, deals, and activities. Look for[managed database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) support with relational features.
- **Authentication and permissions** : CRM solutions should support user roles so sales reps see their own deals while managers access team-wide data.
- **Integration options** : Check whether the platform connects with email, calendar, payment processors, and the tools teams already use.
- **Deployment and hosting** : Determine whether managed hosting or self-hosting is needed, and whether mobile access matters for field teams.
- **AI billing model** : Some builders charge separately for AI usage during development. Others let teams use existing AI subscriptions.
- **Code ownership** : Decide whether source code export and ownership are needed or whether a hosted platform works.


The distinction between "AI CRM software" and "AI app builders for CRM" matters. Pre-built CRMs with AI features typically use predefined data models that may limit customization. AI app builders can generate software tailored to more specific processes.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development, while Floot provides managed infrastructure for working web and mobile applications. Available building capabilities depend on the AI client's connector permissions.


For CRM development, Floot combines conversational building with managed Postgres, authentication, file storage, backend services, and hosting. Teams can describe their sales workflows and use the connected assistant to develop applications without manually assembling separate infrastructure services.


### **Why It Fits CRM Teams**


Floot lets businesses build through an AI assistant they already use rather than requiring a second AI building subscription. Through the[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , supported assistants can create projects, edit TypeScript and React files, provision databases, test functionality, and publish applications.


For CRM specifically, teams can describe their sales pipeline, contact management needs, and reporting requirements in natural language. The AI assistant helps generate the data model, user interface, and backend logic, while Floot provides the infrastructure needed to run the application.


This approach is useful for non-technical founders and operators who need working CRM software with persistent records, user accounts, and ongoing development capabilities.


### **CRM-Relevant Capabilities**


- **Managed database** :[Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) with SQL access and a browser-based table view for contacts, companies, deals, and activities.
- **Authentication** : Built-in[user authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) with email/password login and brokered Google/Microsoft OAuth.
- **File storage** : Storage for customer documents, contracts, and attachments.
- **Notifications** : Email and push notification capabilities for deal updates and task reminders.
- **Scheduled workflows** :[Scheduled jobs](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/jobs) for daily reports and data synchronization, available in published applications on paid plans.
- **Payments** :[Stripe integration](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) for checkout and subscriptions. Live payments require Pro or Power. Floot charges a 1% transaction fee on Pro and 0% on Power, with Stripe processing fees applying separately.
- **Mobile applications** :[Mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android using native shells around the web application.
- **Code ownership** : Ownership of application code, data, and intellectual property on every plan, with full project ZIP export available on paid plans.


### **Why Floot Leads for CRM Teams**


Floot combines conversational development with the infrastructure needed to operate custom CRM applications. Teams can continue refining their software through supported AI assistants while Floot manages hosting, databases, authentication, and deployment.


Floot is **free to start** , with three monthly subscription plans:


- **Free ($0/month)** : 100 build actions per day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting allowance.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and custom domains.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily build actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance.


Floot's current mobile documentation also lists 2 mobile builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Google Play integration requires a paid plan. App store publishing requires separate Apple or Google developer accounts and remains subject to store review.


Hosting usage beyond the included allowance draws from prepaid hosting credit. Optional auto-reload is off by default.


Backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2025), Floot is particularly relevant for businesses that want a working CRM without independently managing databases, hosting services, and authentication infrastructure.


## **2. MindStudio (Remy)**


MindStudio offers a spec-driven development approach through Remy, its product agent for building full-stack applications.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Spec-driven development** : Editable plain-language specifications that compile into full-stack applications
- **Multi-model access** : 200+ AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google without managing separate API keys
- **Specialist agents** : Six sub-agents handling coding, design, roadmap, QA, architecture, and research


### **Key Features**


- Backend, database, frontend, authentication, tests, and deployment included
- Full code ownership with export capabilities
- When requirements change, the specification can be used to regenerate application code without starting over
- Comprehensive infrastructure for building complete applications


### **Considerations**


MindStudio fits teams that want control over their development specification and expect to iterate as their sales process evolves. MindStudio says Remy typically builds an application in 30 to 60 minutes depending on complexity. Remy's availability and pricing should be checked separately from MindStudio's general AI agent subscriptions.


## **3. YouWare**


YouWare generates React applications with built-in backend infrastructure from natural language descriptions.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Custom applications** : Builds an app based on your requirements rather than template-based solutions
- **Full code ownership** : Code export on eligible paid plans for self-hosting and reducing vendor lock-in
- **Visual editing** : Tweaks possible without touching code


### **Key Features**


- AI-generated React applications with YouBase backend
- Code export for self-hosting on supported paid plans
- Remix capabilities to build on existing CRM projects
- Database, authentication, and storage included


### **Considerations**


YouWare fits teams that have outgrown templates and need custom CRM software. A customer example describes an oil and gas founder using YouWare to build a company website and an early internal management portal.


The Pro plan costs $20/month and includes 3,000 AI credits. Higher-tier pricing and credit allowances depend on the current subscription offering.


## **4. Airtable + AI**


Airtable combines spreadsheet familiarity with database capabilities and AI-powered automation features.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Spreadsheet interface** : Database functionality with familiar spreadsheet navigation
- **AI field population** : AI features can fill, summarize, and categorize records at scale
- **Multiple views** : Grid, kanban, calendar, timeline, and gallery views of the same data


### **Key Features**


- Linked records and rollups for contact-to-company relationships
- AI-powered field population and record categorization
- Strong API for custom extensions
- Template gallery with CRM starting points


### **Considerations**


Airtable fits teams that want database-first CRM capabilities with familiar interfaces. Airtable reports that more than 500,000 companies use its platform. The Free tier supports 1,000 records per base, while Team costs $20/user/month and Business costs $45/user/month when billed annually.


## **5. Taskade Genesis**


Taskade Genesis offers prompt-to-CRM generation with embedded AI agents and multiple project views from a single prompt.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Rapid generation** : Generating CRM applications through natural-language prompts, with development time depending on the application's complexity
- **AI agents** : Embedded agents that can act on data, not just store it
- **Multi-view flexibility** : Board, Table, Calendar, Mind Map, and Gantt views


### **Key Features**


- Multi-view projects including Board, Table, Calendar, Mind Map, and Gantt
- Embedded AI agents for automation
- 100+ integrations with services including Gmail, Slack, Zoom, and Stripe
- MCP support for connecting external AI tools


### **Considerations**


Taskade fits teams that want prompt-based CRM creation and multi-view flexibility. Its Pro plan is listed at $20/month with monthly billing, with annual subscription discounts available. The plan supports up to 10 users and includes AI credits for application generation, agents, and automations. Usage limits depend on the selected subscription.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble provides visual programming capabilities for teams that need complex custom logic in their CRM.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual programming** : Supports complex workflows through visual programming
- **Complex logic** : Multi-step approval chains, custom calculators, or industry-specific logic
- **Large user base** : Bubble reports that builders have created more than 8 million apps on its platform


### **Key Features**


- Visual programming for complex business logic
- Full database with custom data types and relations
- Marketplace of plugins including OpenAI, Pinecone, and Stripe
- Managed hosting included


### **Considerations**


Bubble fits teams willing to invest time learning visual programming in exchange for deep customization. Learning time depends on the complexity of CRM workflows. For web-only plans billed monthly, Starter costs $39/month, Growth costs $134/month, and Team costs $399/month.


## **7. Softr**


Softr focuses on AI-powered app building for client-facing portals and internal tools connected to existing data sources.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Client portals** : Customer-facing CRM portals on top of existing data
- **Multiple data sources** : Connections to Airtable, Google Sheets, or HubSpot, or Softr's own database
- **AI Co-Builder** : Generates applications and underlying data structures from plain-language descriptions


### **Key Features**


- AI Co-Builder for prompt-based app generation
- Connections to Airtable, Google Sheets, and HubSpot as data sources
- Authentication and permissions for client-facing portals
- Custom domains on all paid plans


### **Considerations**


Softr works well for teams building customer-facing CRM portals using existing sources such as Airtable, Google Sheets, or HubSpot, or Softr's own database. Its AI Co-Builder generates applications and underlying data structures from plain-language descriptions.


Softr's Basic plan costs $25/month, Pro costs $119/month, and Business costs $395/month when billed monthly, with lower effective monthly prices available through annual billing.


## **8. Glide**


Glide provides mobile-friendly business applications, with Glide Classic supporting progressive web applications and GlideOS offering a separate AI-driven app-building experience.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Mobile-first** : PWAs that provide mobile-friendly application experiences
- **Field sales focus** : Interfaces for sales representatives who work primarily from phones
- **Progressive web apps** : Browser-based applications that do not require app store downloads


### **Key Features**


- Mobile-first PWA output through Glide Classic
- Glide Agent for prompt-based app generation, with availability depending on the account
- AI columns for classification and enrichment
- Mobile-friendly interfaces for field teams with connectivity-dependent data synchronization
- Google Sheets integration on eligible plans


### **Considerations**


Glide fits teams where mobile access is the primary use case. The platform provides mobile-friendly CRM interfaces, although reliable connectivity is needed for normal data synchronization and workflows.


Glide reports that more than 100,000 companies use its platform. For Glide Classic, Explorer starts at $19/month, Maker at $49/month, and Business at $199/month when billed annually. GlideOS is a separate product with its own pricing structure.


## **9. Lovable**


Lovable generates React code with managed backend options, including Supabase Postgres, for teams that want source-code ownership.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Real code generation** : Generates React code rather than proprietary formats
- **Code portability** : Supports code export and independent hosting
- **Backend options** : Managed backend capabilities, including Supabase-based infrastructure


### **Key Features**


- React code generation
- Supabase Postgres backend integration
- Source code ownership and export
- Developer community and integration ecosystem


### **Considerations**


Lovable fits teams seeking React-based CRM applications with source-code ownership and the option to use managed hosting or deploy independently. Teams should evaluate how database configuration, authentication, deployment, and maintenance fit their intended CRM workflows.


## **10. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new provides browser-based AI code generation with integrated deployment capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based** : Prompt-to-deployment workflows entirely in the browser
- **No setup required** : No local development environment needed
- **Integrated deployment** : Deployment workflows available from the platform


### **Key Features**


- Browser-based development environment
- Integrated deployment capabilities
- Database and authentication support
- Built on StackBlitz WebContainers technology


### **Considerations**


Bolt.new fits teams that want to move from prompt to a deployed CRM in the browser without local development setup. Teams should assess the backend services, deployment configuration, and ongoing maintenance requirements for their specific application.


## **11. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent combines an established development platform with AI agent capabilities for full-stack application building.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Established platform** : Replit reports more than 60 million users worldwide
- **Automatic provisioning** : Can provision data and hosting for applications
- **Full IDE** : Development environment with terminal access


### **Key Features**


- AI agent that provisions data and hosting
- Full IDE with terminal access
- Established platform infrastructure
- Educational resources for application development


### **Considerations**


Replit fits teams that want a full development environment alongside AI agent capabilities and value its community resources. Teams developing CRM applications should consider their preferred level of control over code, deployment, debugging, and infrastructure configuration.


## **12. Base44**


Base44 offers AI-generated full-stack applications with managed data storage and hosting, and operates as a Wix-owned platform.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full-stack generation** : Generates application pages, data models, and backend functionality together
- **Persistent records** : Makes it an option for custom CRMs that need persistent records and user authentication
- **Wix backing** : Platform acquired by Wix in 2025


### **Key Features**


- Built-in application data storage using managed entities
- Full-stack application generation
- Authentication included
- Managed application hosting and deployment


### **Considerations**


Base44 fits teams that need custom CRM applications with persistent records and managed backend functionality. Businesses should evaluate how its generated data structures, available integrations, and deployment controls align with their sales and customer management requirements.


## **13. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible ChatGPT subscribers create, preview, and publish interactive websites and lightweight applications through natural-language conversations.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational building** : App creation and editing inside ChatGPT through conversation
- **Lightweight applications** : Supports lightweight CRM workflows such as lead tracking, internal dashboards, and customer information tools
- **Persistent storage** : Supports persistent databases and file storage


### **Key Features**


- Conversational app creation and editing inside ChatGPT
- Hosted websites and interactive applications
- Persistent data storage and database support
- Sharing and access controls
- Connections to supported external services


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites fits teams that want to build lightweight CRM applications directly within ChatGPT. Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting and storage have separate limits.


For businesses that prefer managed Postgres infrastructure, integrated Stripe payments, and iOS or Android app publishing workflows, Floot offers a separate full-stack solution that also works through supported ChatGPT configurations.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for CRM Software Development**


Floot stands out as a practical choice for non-technical founders and operators who want CRM software with persistent data and managed infrastructure. Its MCP connector allows development through supported AI assistants, while Floot handles the underlying services needed to run and publish applications.


Its[full-stack infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) supports essential CRM requirements:


- **Managed Postgres** for contacts, companies, deals, activities, and relational customer data.
- **Built-in authentication** for team logins, with application-level permissions configurable through the generated code.
- **File storage** for contracts, customer documents, and attachments.
- **Email and push notifications** for customer communications, deal updates, and reminders.
- **Scheduled workflows** for recurring reports and data synchronization in published applications on paid plans.
- **Web and mobile publishing** with custom domains on paid plans and managed mobile packaging workflows.


The[community showcase](https://floot.com/en/showcase) includes business-management, real estate, and CRM-related projects. Floot is free to start, and its paid plans provide higher building-action allowances and recurring hosting allowances. For teams already using a supported AI assistant, it provides a way to develop and operate custom CRM software without assembling separate backend and hosting services.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can a non-technical person build custom CRM software using an AI app builder?**


Yes. Modern AI app builders let non-technical users describe their sales processes, contact management requirements, and reporting workflows in plain language. A connected AI assistant can help generate the data model, user interface, backend logic, and functionality needed for a custom CRM. Floot supports this approach through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , which works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot handles managed infrastructure while the connected assistant performs development. Available building actions depend on the client's permissions. Users should still test generated workflows, permissions, and data handling before deploying their CRM.


### **How much does it cost to build CRM software with an AI app builder?**


Costs vary by platform, subscription tier, hosting usage, AI consumption, and team size. Some platforms charge per user, while others use subscription-based or usage-based pricing. Floot is free to start with 100 daily build actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting allowance. Pro costs $25/month with 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Power costs $100/month with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance. Hosting usage beyond the allowance draws from prepaid credit, with optional auto-reload. Scheduled jobs require a paid plan and a published app. Building through supported assistants does not use Floot AI credits for standard connector operations, although the connected AI service may have its own charges or limits. Check[current pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) before subscribing.


### **What CRM functionalities can be built with AI app builders?**


AI app builders can help create contact management systems, deal pipelines, activity tracking, task management, lead assignment, reporting dashboards, and custom sales workflows. Depending on the platform, teams can also add email notifications, file attachments, customer portals, payment processing, and integrations with other business tools.


Floot's[managed database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) supports relational data structures for contacts, companies, deals, and activities. Its infrastructure also supports authentication, storage, scheduled jobs, and external API integrations. These capabilities allow businesses to design CRM applications around their processes rather than relying entirely on predefined templates.


### **Do AI app builders provide hosting and deployment for CRM software?**


Many AI app builders provide managed hosting, although deployment options and included resources vary. Floot hosts published CRM applications on its managed infrastructure and provides a *.floot.app subdomain. Custom domains are available on paid plans, and hosting consumption is metered against the account's available allowance and prepaid credit. Floot also supports native iOS and Android app packaging through its[mobile publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) workflow. Its current mobile documentation lists 2 builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. App store distribution requires separate Apple or Google developer accounts, Google Play integration requires a paid Floot plan, and final approval remains with the stores.


### **Can existing CRM data be integrated with an AI-built application?**


Yes. Many AI app builders support database imports, API connections, or integrations with existing business systems. Moving contacts, companies, deals, and activity records into a custom CRM typically involves exporting the existing data, mapping fields, checking relationships, and validating the migrated records. Floot provides managed Postgres with database export available on every plan and database import available on paid plans. External services can also connect through documented APIs and integration workflows. Businesses should plan the migration carefully, verify customer permissions, and test the resulting CRM before relying on it for daily operations.
